title: Simplify My Health Buddy UI flow, rename helper to Luma, add location step, and fix Grown-ups gate

requirements.text: Rename the helper character from “Amanda” to “Luma” everywhere in the app, and update the greeting copy to exactly: “Hi, I’m Luma. I help you show how you feel.”

quotes:
Change the character name from “Amanda” to Luma everywhere in the app.
Greeting should say:
“Hi, I’m Luma. I help you show how you feel.”

acceptanceCriteria: No screen shows the name “Amanda”.
Welcome greeting text matches exactly: “Hi, I’m Luma. I help you show how you feel.”

requirements.text: Simplify supportive wording by replacing the specified longer sentences with the specified short phrases wherever they appear in the app UI.

quotes:
“Thank you for telling me. Let’s tell a grown-up together.” → “Let’s tell a grown-up”
“Well done for telling someone. That was a brave thing to do.” → “You did the right thing 💛”

acceptanceCriteria: The helper message on the feeling confirmation screen uses “Let’s tell a grown-up”.
The encouragement shown on the adult message flow uses exactly: “You did the right thing 💛”.
No remaining UI text contains the two long sentences provided in the request.

requirements.text: Improve the first screen so it only shows: (1) the logo, (2) the Luma character, and (3) one large “Start” button. Move all other menu options to a separate next screen that appears after “Start” is pressed.

quotes:
The first screen should only show:
Logo
Luma character
One large button: Start Move all other menu options to the next screen after Start is pressed.

acceptanceCriteria: On app launch (after splash), the user sees only the logo, the Luma character, and a single large “Start” button (no other menu buttons).
Pressing “Start” navigates to a new menu screen that contains the previously available options (e.g., feelings, energy check, daily feelings, feel better, and grown-ups access).
The overall navigation still allows reaching all existing features from the new post-Start menu screen.

requirements.text: Make the “Show this to an adult” button the largest and most visually prominent button in the entire app, and center it on its screen.

quotes:
Make the “Show this to an adult” button the largest button in the app.
Center it on screen and make it stand out more than all other buttons.

acceptanceCriteria: On the feeling confirmation screen, “Show this to an adult” is centered and visually dominant compared to any other button in the app (larger size and stronger emphasis styling).
No other screen contains a button that is larger or more visually emphasized than “Show this to an adult”.

requirements.text: Remove scrolling on the feelings selection page by resizing and laying out the feeling option cards evenly so all feeling options are visible on one screen at once.

quotes:
Fit all feeling options onto one screen without scrolling by resizing cards evenly.
Children must see all options at once.

acceptanceCriteria: The feelings page shows all feeling options without requiring vertical scrolling on common mobile viewport sizes.
All feeling option cards are evenly sized and presented in a consistent grid.

requirements.text: Add a new location follow-up screen after the user presses the main help button. The new screen must ask “Where are you?” and provide three large buttons: “At school”, “At home”, “Outside”.

quotes:
After pressing the help button, show a new page asking:
“Where are you?”
Buttons:
At school
At home
Outside

acceptanceCriteria: Pressing “Show this to an adult” navigates to a new location screen instead of directly to the adult message screen.
The location screen displays the question exactly: “Where are you?”
The location screen provides exactly three buttons: “At school”, “At home”, “Outside”.
Selecting any location proceeds to the existing adult message screen flow.

requirements.text: Fix the “Grown-ups only” section so it is a real, working button that opens a lock screen flow: require the user to press-and-hold a star for 3 seconds and then answer a simple math question (e.g., 7 + 3). Show the exact error message “Try again, grown-ups only” on wrong answer and open the settings page on correct answer. If press-and-hold is not supported, require only the math question before access.

quotes:
Make “Grown-ups only” a real working button (not just an image).
When tapped, open a lock screen:
User must press and hold the star for 3 seconds
Then answer a simple maths question (example: 7 + 3)
Wrong answer shows: “Try again, grown-ups only”
Correct answer opens the settings page
If press-and-hold is not supported, require only the maths question before access.

acceptanceCriteria: Tapping “Grown-ups only” opens a dedicated lock UI (not immediate navigation into settings).
When press-and-hold is supported, the lock UI requires a continuous 3-second hold on a star before showing the math question.
When press-and-hold is not supported, the lock UI directly shows the math question without requiring hold.
Submitting a wrong math answer shows exactly: “Try again, grown-ups only” (and does not grant access).
Submitting the correct math answer grants access and navigates to the grown-ups settings area page.

requirements.text: Ensure all updated and new screens maintain a calm, simple, child-friendly presentation with short, easy-to-understand English UI text.

quotes: The app must remain calm, simple, child-friendly and easy to understand

acceptanceCriteria: All new/modified UI strings are short, supportive, and in English.
No new screen introduces dense paragraphs or complex instructions beyond what is necessary for the lock flow.

constraints: Do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui (compose them instead).
Do not edit immutable hook paths: frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx.
Keep backend as a single Motoko actor; only introduce backend changes if strictly required (these UI changes should be achievable fully on the frontend).
nonGoals: Add external authentication providers beyond Internet Identity.
Add external databases or third-party integrations.
